identity.title: Recent advances in design strategies for rapid mycoplasma detection: Towards point-of-care testing.

content.abstract: Mycoplasma pathogens present significant challenges for clinical point-of-care testing (POCT) due to their pathogenicity, public health implications, and the limitations of conventional detection methods. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in rapid mycoplasma detection technologies, with emphasis on sensing design principles, technical bottlenecks, innovative solutions, and clinical performance. Three major technology systems are comprehensively discussed: (1) Molecular diagnostic platforms, focusing on optimization strategies for non-CRISPR isothermal amplification and CRISPR/Cas-based systems that leverage collateral cleavage for ultra-sensitive detection; (2) Emerging biosensing technologies, encompassing colorimetric, fluorescence, and electrochemical modalities, with detailed analysis of transducer functionalization and signal transduction mechanisms; and (3) Lateral flow assays (LFAs), highlighting innovative signal amplification strategies for rapid nucleic acid and antigen/antibody testing. Furthermore, the integration of mass spectrometry (MS) with metabolomics for high-throughput metabolic profiling is examined. Finally, we discuss the core challenges of mycoplasma POCT, including sample preparation, matching detection technologies to the unique biological traits of Mycoplasma, and use cases such as at-home testing. Building on these challenges, we also outline future prospects: discrimination between viable and non-viable organisms, resistance-informed testing, and device-level integration. These insights collectively define a roadmap for next-generation 'sample-to-answer' POCT devices. This review aims to bridge the gap between laboratory innovation and clinical diagnostics for mycoplasma management.
